title: After the backup key is changed, the nightly job never re-encrypts the environment variables to the new key, so the only env/ copy still needs the old private key
steps: 1. Night 1: nightly.sh runs with BACKUP_AGE_PUBLIC_KEY = key A; env/angelone-env-<t>.txt.age and state/env-fingerprint.txt are written. 2. Follow docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md 'Changing the backup key' step 2: replace the secret with key B and run the workflow by hand. 3. Look at env/ in the bucket and try to decrypt every object with key B.
expected: The run after a key change uploads a fresh env/ copy encrypted to the new key (the runbook says to change the key 'if the private key may have been exposed, or when the holders change' and to run the workflow by hand, which implies everything current is then under the new key).
actual: The job prints 'Environment variables are unchanged since the last copy; not uploaded.' The fingerprint in state/ is only the SHA-256 of the variables and does not include the recipient. The newest env/ copy (JWT signing key, JWKS, CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, Resend and SSO secrets) stays encrypted only to the old key until some variable happens to change. If the key was changed because the old private key was lost or its holder left, a restore to a new deployment cannot recover the environment variables; the daily exports open with key B but the stored FAA/Spruce/SSO credentials inside them need CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY from the env file.
evidence: Repro output: 'Environment variables are unchanged since the last copy; not uploaded.' then 'env/ objects: 1; daily objects: 2' and no env/ object opens with key B. scripts/backup/nightly.sh:279-297 (fingerprint = sha256 of env.txt only); docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md:143-149.
repro: repro/ops/zz-hunt-env-not-reencrypted-after-key-change.sh (bash <file> <checkout>; needs age, zip, jq; exits 1 while the bug exists)
notes: Fix options: include the recipient in the fingerprint, or have the runbook tell the operator to delete state/env-fingerprint.txt (it is outside the lock) before the manual run. nightly.test.sh has no key-change case.

title: The hosted sample program seeds its four flights with the start and end meter readings swapped, so each sample flight starts one hour after it ends
steps: 1. On a local backend run `npx convex run sampleProgram:seed '{"email":"<admin>"}'`. 2. Read operations.snapshot (or export and build the records workbook with `npm run backup:workbook`). 3. Look at sample-flight-1..4.
expected: hobbsOff/tachOff (where the flight started, src/domain/model.ts:202-204) equal the aircraft baseline and hobbsOn/tachOn (where it ended) are one hour later, as a real accepted flight is stored (the smoke-test flight: hobbsOff 100 h, hobbsOn 101 h).
actual: sampleProgram.ts writes hobbsOn: a.seconds and hobbsOff: a.seconds + HOUR. The Flight log sheet of the records workbook shows SAMPLE-1 'Hobbs start 1201, Hobbs end 1200, Hours 0' (same for SAMPLE-2..4), while the aircraft total is 1201 h. The training program an inspector or new user is shown first has four accepted flights with negative duration.
notes: Found while checking the workbook against the export; outside the ops area proper. Sample data only, every record is marked fictional. Run: node zz-hunt-ops/readxlsx.mjs is not kept; any xlsx reader shows it.

title: Running `npm run setup:auth` again on production without SITE_URL in the shell silently replaces the production SITE_URL with http://localhost:5173
steps: 1. `SITE_URL=https://ops.example.test node scripts/configure-auth.mjs` (first set-up). 2. Later run `npm run setup:auth` again with the same deployment selected and no SITE_URL in the shell (for example to check the keys, or following README step 2 with the production deploy key still exported). 3. `npx convex env get SITE_URL`.
expected: A script that says it is 'Safe to repeat: a key that exists is kept' also keeps an existing SITE_URL, or refuses to fall back to the localhost default when the selected deployment is production (CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY starts with prod:).
actual: Prints 'Existing signing key retained. Existing credential encryption key retained. Site URL configured.' and SITE_URL is now http://localhost:5173. On production that breaks Google/Microsoft sign-in redirects and puts localhost links in alert and password emails until someone notices. No warning is printed.
evidence: Local run on the hunt-9 backend (port 3230): env get SITE_URL returned https://ops.example.test, then http://localhost:5173 after the second run. scripts/configure-auth.mjs:19-22. The incident runbook mentions the default in one table cell (docs/runbooks/incident-response.md:69) but README.md:189-193 shows the bare command.
notes: Related, unproven: if `env set JWT_PRIVATE_KEY` succeeds and `env set JWKS` then fails, a rerun prints 'Existing signing key retained' and never sets JWKS (isSet checks only JWT_PRIVATE_KEY), configure-auth.mjs:27-41. admin:bootstrap and the First-time setup workflow are safe to repeat: both refuse once a user exists, and the workflow checks before it changes anything.

title: .gitignore does not cover the secret files the backup runbook tells the operator to create in the checkout: the age private key, the decrypted environment variables and the downloaded archives
steps: 1. In a checkout run `git check-ignore -v key.txt new-key.txt env.txt angelone-env-20261101T084109Z.txt angelone-20261104T084112Z.zip.age angelone-20261104T084112Z.manifest.json`. 2. Compare with docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md lines 82-83, 95-119 and 147, and go-live-checklist.md line 40, which create exactly these files and run `scripts/backup/decrypt.sh key.txt angelone-...zip.age` (a path relative to the repository root).
expected: Every file the runbook has the operator write next to the repository during a restore or key change is git-ignored, as .env*, /*.zip and /*.xlsx already are, so `git add -A` during an incident cannot stage the backup private key or the production JWT signing key and credentials key.
actual: git check-ignore matches none of key.txt, new-key.txt, env.txt, angelone-env-<time>.txt (the decrypted production variables), *.age or *.manifest.json. Only the decrypted .zip and the .xlsx are ignored. The CI gitleaks job would report an age or PEM key only after it was pushed.
evidence: Output of git check-ignore in the hunt-9 worktree: 'NOT IGNORED' for all six names; .gitignore:1-37; docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md:82-83,95-119,147; docs/go-live-checklist.md:40
notes: Either ignore these names (key.txt, *-key.txt, env.txt, angelone-env-*.txt, *.age, *.manifest.json at the root) or have the runbook work in a directory outside the repository.

title: The '36-hour' stale-backup warning cannot be sent until about 52 hours after the last good copy, so one failed nightly backup is never reported by the app
steps: 1. The nightly backup runs at 08:41 UTC (.github/workflows/backup.yml:18); the only place the app evaluates the 36-hour rule and tells anyone is the daily digest at 13:00 UTC (convex/crons.ts:24-29, convex/alerts.ts:261-279). 2. Monday's backup completes 08:45 UTC. Tuesday's run fails. 3. Tuesday 13:00 UTC digest: offsiteFreshness({completedAt: Mon 08:45}, Tue 13:00).
expected: The first digest after a missed night warns system administrators (the runbook and ADR-0008 present the app warning as the safety net that 'also catches a schedule that stopped running').
actual: The copy is 28 h 15 min old, status 'ok', no warning. The first warning is Wednesday 13:00 UTC, 52 hours after the last good copy and after two missed nights. It also needs RESEND_API_KEY and RESEND_FROM (alerts:sendDigests returns {skipped:true} without them, verified on the local backend) and an administrator who opted in to the digest; backup-restore.md 'Who is told when it fails' mentions neither Resend nor the delay.
evidence: repro/ops/zz-hunt-backup-warning-timing.test.ts fails with: expected 'ok' to be 'stale'. src/domain/offsiteBackups.ts:14, convex/alerts.ts:255-264, convex/crons.ts:24-29, docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md:59
repro: repro/ops/zz-hunt-backup-warning-timing.test.ts (copy to src/domain/, then npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-backup-warning-timing.test.ts)
notes: A limit of about 26 hours (one period plus slack for GitHub's late starts), or evaluating shortly after the backup window, would report a single missed night the same day. GitHub's failure email and the optional Better Stack heartbeat are the only same-day signals.

title: Deploy releases whatever commit a green CI run on main names, with no check that it is the newest: re-running an old CI or Deploy run puts old backend functions and an old website over production
steps: 1. Commits A then B are merged to main; both deploy. 2. Someone opens the week-old CI run for A and clicks 'Re-run all jobs' (to check a flaky test), or re-runs/approves the old Deploy run for A. 3. CI for A finishes green: GitHub sends workflow_run completed with head_sha = A, event = push, head_branch = main.
expected: Deploy refuses a commit that is behind what production already runs (for example: DEPLOY_SHA must equal the tip of origin/main, or main's tip must not be a descendant of it).
actual: The job condition (deploy.yml:40-46) passes, and 'Require a commit on main' only tests `git merge-base --is-ancestor $DEPLOY_SHA origin/main` (deploy.yml:73-78), which is true for every old commit. The run then executes `npx convex deploy` and `wrangler deploy` for A: functions added in B disappear, the older schema is pushed if the stored documents still satisfy it, and the older site goes live, with no backup confirmation because auto runs skip that step. Without required reviewers (the runbook says GitHub Free private repositories cannot have them) nothing asks a person first.
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml:40-46,52-53,61-78,131; docs/runbooks/release.md:127 ('Convex has no rollback command'). Read from the workflow; GitHub Actions cannot be run in this environment.
notes: The same gap lets a late approval of an older queued Deploy run land after a newer one. A one-line guard: fail unless "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" = "$DEPLOY_SHA" for workflow_run events.

title: A manual Deploy run from main does not look at CI at all: it releases a commit whose browser tests, secret scan, dependency audit or backup-job tests are red or still running
steps: 1. A commit lands on main and CI fails (for example the gitleaks or npm audit job, or a Playwright test), so no automatic deploy starts. 2. Actions > Deploy > Run workflow > main, tick the backup box.
expected: The workflow confirms the commit has a successful CI run (the runbook's release checklist says 'CI is green on the main commit you are releasing'), or the runbook and workflow header say plainly that the manual path skips those gates.
actual: For workflow_dispatch the only conditions are ref == main and the backup tick box (deploy.yml:41,55-59). The job repeats `npm run check` only; the e2e suite with production headers, test:backup, the audit and the secret scan are never consulted. release.md:18 says of the security gates 'either one failing also holds back Deploy', which is true only for the automatic path.
notes: Could query the check runs for github.sha with the read-only token before deploying. Workflow logic only; not executed.

title: `npm run check:standards` says 'all clear' for work that is not committed yet, and for code file types it has no comment style for
steps: 1. In a checkout create an untracked file zz/bad.ts containing a TypeScript ignore comment and no header (or edit a tracked file the same way without committing). 2. Run `npm run check:standards`. 3. Run `node .claude/hooks/check-standards.mjs zz/bad.ts` for comparison. 4. Also pass a Dockerfile, a .toml, a .mts file with a TypeScript ignore comment, and a .py file with '# ruff: noqa' and '# pyright: ignore' lines.
expected: The command CONSTRAINTS.md section 9 and CLAUDE.md step 5 tell people and agents to run 'before saying the work is done' checks the files they just changed, including uncommitted and untracked ones; a suppression in any code file is reported.
actual: Step 2 prints 'Engineering standards: 4 file(s) checked, all clear.' and exits 0: changedFiles() runs `git diff --name-only <ref> HEAD`, which lists committed changes only. Step 3 reports both problems for the same file. Step 4 exits 0: extensions outside COMMENT_STYLE_BY_EXTENSION (.mts, .cts, .toml, .jsonc, Dockerfile, public/_headers) are skipped before the suppression scan, and the Python rules miss the 'ruff: noqa', 'flake8: noqa' and 'pyright: ignore' spellings. Files written through the shell are not seen by the edit hook either (CONSTRAINTS.md section 11), so only CI catches them, after the push.
evidence: Run in the hunt-9 worktree: check:standards exit 0 with an untracked bad .ts present; direct call reported 'missing the architectural header block' and 'line 2: TypeScript suppression comment'. .claude/hooks/check-standards.mjs:28-43 (extension map), 70-77 (rules), 244-252 (git diff against HEAD), 223-231 (style null returns before suppressionProblems). Tracked files of unmapped types today: .devcontainer/Dockerfile, .gitleaks.toml, wrangler.jsonc, public/_headers.
notes: Separate from the two known gaps (RM-06 shellcheck, RM-41 ref tip). Possibly related and not proven: `git diff --name-only` quotes non-ASCII file names unless core.quotepath is off, so such a file would be looked up under a quoted name, not found, and skipped silently (readCheckableText returns null for a missing file).

title: The release runbook tells the operator to run `memberships:backfill` with the production deploy key after every deploy, while the README and the go-live checklist say a fresh deployment must skip it
steps: 1. Read docs/runbooks/release.md 'After every deploy' (lines 90-100). 2. Read README.md 'One-off steps for deployments with older data' (lines 300-310) and docs/go-live-checklist.md line 27.
expected: One instruction. Since production started empty on 2026-11-03 and Deploy now runs on every green merge, the runbook should not ask for the production deploy key to be typed into a shell after each of them.
actual: release.md: 'Run the one-off commands from the README Deployment section against production ... npx convex run memberships:backfill' after every deploy. README: 'Fresh deployments skip this section ... the step below has nothing to do there.' Checklist: 'the README's one-off data-repair commands are not needed on a fresh deployment'. Run locally the command is a harmless no-op ({isDone: true}), so the cost is an unnecessary handling of the production deploy key on every release. The same section's 'Release' steps describe only the manual run ('tick the backup box'); with auto-deploy the 'Before you start' backup has to happen before the merge, which the section does not say.
evidence: docs/runbooks/release.md:80-100; README.md:300-310; docs/go-live-checklist.md:27; local run of `npx convex run memberships:backfill` returned {isDone:true, synced:2}
notes: All relative links and anchors in docs/runbooks, docs/*.md, docs/adr, README, CONTEXT, SECURITY and the checklist resolve (72 files checked by script). The documented commands audit:recordManualEntry, secretsMigration:reseal and memberships:backfill exist and ran on the local backend.

title: The nightly job stores any valid ZIP with one document as a good backup: it does not check that file storage or the expected tables are in the export
steps: 1. Run scripts/backup/nightly.sh against a Convex CLI whose export ZIP holds only users/documents.jsonl (no _storage folder, no other table), as the fake CLI in repro/ops/zz-hunt-env-not-reencrypted-after-key-change.sh does. 2. Read the result.
expected: A partial export (the --include-file-storage part missing, or far fewer tables or documents than the previous night's manifest) fails the run or at least warns, because the app records the copy as good and the heartbeat is pinged.
actual: The run succeeds, uploads daily/ and monthly/, records the copy and prints Done. The only content checks are `unzip -t` and 'more than zero documents outside system tables' (nightly.sh:197-210). The manifest's per-table counts are written but never compared with anything.
evidence: Both runs in the OP-1 repro succeed with a one-table export that has no _storage folder; scripts/backup/nightly.sh:197-210
repro: repro/ops/zz-hunt-env-not-reencrypted-after-key-change.sh (shows a one-table export without _storage being accepted twice)
notes: Hardening: require _storage/documents.jsonl and the core tables (users, aircraft, audit) to be present; compare counts with the previous manifest. The real export from the local backend did contain all 59 tables and the 5 stored files.

title: The app records each backup with the encrypted object's size but the plaintext ZIP's SHA-256, while the function's contract says the hash is the encrypted object's
steps: 1. Read convex/backups.ts:31-33 ('@param bytes - The encrypted object's size. @param sha256 - Its SHA-256'). 2. Read scripts/backup/nightly.sh:303-312 (bytes: $enc_bytes, sha256: $plain_sha) and nightly.test.sh:311 ('recorded sha256 is the plaintext ZIP's').
expected: The stored hash and its documentation agree, so someone checking an R2 object against the backupRuns row knows which file to hash.
actual: backupRuns.sha256 is the hash of the decrypted ZIP; hashing the .zip.age object in R2 never matches it. The manifest holds both hashes correctly.
notes: Wording fix only; the value is not shown in the UI.

title: Deploy and the documented rollback run wrangler through `npx --yes wrangler@4.151.3`, so everything wrangler depends on is resolved fresh at release time with the Cloudflare token in the environment; two scripts also import esbuild, which package.json does not declare
steps: 1. Read .github/workflows/deploy.yml:146-155 and 157-171. 2. Run `npm ls esbuild` and read scripts/bootstrap-admin.mjs:11 and scripts/backup/records-workbook.mjs:16.
expected: Every tool that runs with production credentials comes from package-lock.json (integrity-checked, covered by Dependabot's 7-day cooldown and the npm audit job), as the Convex CLI does.
actual: Only wrangler's own version is pinned. Its dependency tree (miniflare, workerd, esbuild and others) is installed by npx at run time from whatever satisfies its ranges that minute, outside the lockfile, the audit job and the cooldown, in a step that holds CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN. esbuild is present only because convex and vite bring it (`npm ls esbuild`: convex@1.49.0 > esbuild@0.27.0); First-time setup (bootstrap-admin.mjs) and the nightly Dropbox step (records-workbook.mjs) stop working if a dependency update drops or un-hoists it.
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml:29-32,152-155,171; scripts/bootstrap-admin.mjs:11; scripts/backup/records-workbook.mjs:16; package.json (no wrangler, no esbuild)
notes: Adding wrangler and esbuild as devDependencies and calling `npx wrangler` after npm ci would put both under the lockfile. Also noted: scripts/check-csp-origin.mjs accepts a Convex URL with a non-default port (https://x.convex.cloud:8443 passes) although the CSP source https://*.convex.cloud only covers port 443; not reachable with real Convex URLs.
